hints: At time T, machine i makes floor(T/k_i) products.
The total product count is monotone: once enough products are made by T, every larger time also works.
Binary-search the smallest feasible T; stop counting early when the target is reached.
analogy: Ask whether a proposed time is enough, then shrink the time range like a guessing game.
algorithm: Binary-search T from 0 to min(k)*t. Feasibility sums floor(T/k_i), capped when it reaches t; find the first feasible time.
correctness: The predicate changes only from false to true as time grows; binary search finds its boundary, which is exactly the minimum time required.
complexity: O(n log U) time and O(1) extra space, where U=min(k_i)*t.
example: Machines taking 3,2,5 seconds make floor(8/3)+floor(8/2)+floor(8/5)=2+4+1=7 products by time 8, so 8 seconds is feasible.
